notes.Victor Wembanyama: San Antonio is without Dylan Harper (left hip strain, one to three weeks) and Tobias Harris (left calf strain), so more of the offense runs through him, and he has played 33 to 35 minutes in his last three games. New Orleans is on the second night of a back-to-back after Jeremiah Fears, Zion Williamson and Saddiq Bey each played 37 or 38 minutes in Friday's comeback loss at Oklahoma City.
notes.Karl-Anthony Towns: Jordan Clarkson is out with plantar fasciitis and OG Anunoby is questionable with left calf tightness, which leaves more of the frontcourt minutes to Towns; he has played 33 to 43 minutes in his last three games. Portland is without Ja Morant, Shaedon Sharpe and Vit Krejci, and Deni Avdija is questionable with a left foot injury.
notes.Ty Jerome: Ty Jerome is listed as probable. Memphis is short on ball handlers and scorers with Cameron Boozer (ankle), Jerami Grant (calf), Javon Small, Scotty Pippen Jr. and GG Jackson all ruled out, so he should carry a big share of the offense.
notes.Cooper Flagg: Dallas is without Dereck Lively II (foot surgery), and P.J. Washington and Walter Clayton Jr. are both questionable, so Flagg's load could grow further; he played 34 minutes last time out. The Clippers are missing Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram.
notes.Jalen Brunson: With Jordan Clarkson out, New York loses its backup scorer at guard, so more of the bench-unit creation falls to Brunson; he has played 34 to 41 minutes in his last three games. OG Anunoby is questionable with left calf tightness.
notes.Jaylen Wells: Jaylen Wells has started the last three games with Cameron Boozer out, and Jerami Grant is now ruled out too after leaving Thursday's game with a left calf strain. That leaves Memphis thin on the wing, and Wells has played 24 to 27 minutes in that stretch.
notes.Taylor Hendricks: Taylor Hendricks started on Thursday with Cameron Boozer out and has played 19 to 21 minutes in each of his last three games. Jerami Grant's calf strain removes another forward, which opens more minutes for him.
notes.Quinten Post: Quinten Post has played only 6 to 10 minutes in his last three games. Memphis is down Cameron Boozer, Jerami Grant and GG Jackson in the frontcourt, but his role has not grown yet, so his floor is low.
notes.Jordan Poole: Jordan Poole played only 13 minutes on Friday, down from about 30 in his two previous games, because Trey Murphy III returned from his knee injury and took the bench wing minutes. New Orleans has not posted its injury report yet, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Trey Lyles: Minnesota is without Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark, which frees frontcourt and wing minutes. Lyles has played 16 to 31 minutes off the bench in his last three games, so the range is wide.
notes.Landry Shamet: Jordan Clarkson is out with plantar fasciitis, which leaves Shamet as the main bench guard behind Jalen Brunson; he has played 24 to 30 minutes in his last three games.
notes.Isaiah Jackson: The Clippers are without Bradley Beal and Brandon Ingram, but Isaiah Jackson's minutes have bounced from 9 to 19 in his last three games, so his role depends on how the frontcourt rotation shakes out.
notes.Luke Kornet: Luke Kornet is the backup center behind Victor Wembanyama and has played 13 to 15 minutes in each of his last three games. The injuries to Dylan Harper and Tobias Harris are at guard and forward, so they do not add much to his role.
notes.Tyrese Maxey: Tyrese Maxey is questionable with a right foot sprain after a late scratch on Wednesday, his first absence of the season. Jaylen Brown is out again with a left hamstring strain, so if Maxey sits, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope are likely to start again as they did Wednesday.
notes.Anfernee Simons: Anfernee Simons started and played 38 minutes on Wednesday with Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown out. Brown is out again tonight and Maxey is questionable, so another big role is possible.
notes.Joel Embiid: Philadelphia is without Jaylen Brown and may be without Tyrese Maxey (questionable, right foot), so Embiid could carry even more of the offense. He is managing a plantar fascia issue but has played the games since sitting the first night of the Nov. 15-16 back-to-back.
notes.Myles Turner: Myles Turner missed Thursday with a left shoulder contusion but is not on Saturday's injury report, so he should be back in the starting lineup against Philadelphia.
notes.Kyle Kuzma: Kyle Kuzma missed Thursday with a right shoulder contusion but is not on Saturday's injury report, so he should rejoin the rotation against Philadelphia.
notes.Deni Avdija: Deni Avdija is questionable with a left foot contusion after missing the Tuesday and Thursday games, his first absences of the season. If he sits again, Jayson Kent is likely to start for a third straight game.
notes.Jayson Kent: Jayson Kent has started the last two games in place of Deni Avdija, but he played only 17 minutes on Thursday. Avdija is questionable tonight, so Kent's start depends on that status.
notes.OG Anunoby: OG Anunoby is questionable with left calf tightness. With Jordan Clarkson also out, New York's rotation is thinner, so Josh Hart and Landry Shamet would absorb more minutes if Anunoby sits.
notes.Trey Murphy III: Trey Murphy III returned from his knee injury on Friday after missing six games and played 29 minutes off the bench. New Orleans has not posted its injury report yet, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back right after his return.
notes.Jeremiah Fears: Jeremiah Fears played 38 minutes on Friday, up from about 31 in his previous five games, and stayed on the floor through the close finish. New Orleans has not posted its injury report yet, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back.
notes.Zion Williamson: Zion Williamson played 37 minutes on Friday despite early foul trouble, up from 25 and 32 in his previous two games. New Orleans has not posted its injury report yet, and tonight is the second night of a back-to-back, which is worth watching for him.
notes.Cedric Coward: Cedric Coward has started each of Memphis's last three games, and with Cameron Boozer and Jerami Grant both out, he is one of the few healthy forwards left.
